final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is analytically useful, but it does not satisfy the certification standard in the policy text. The admissible evidence supports that the release is not broadly failing on aggregate readiness grounds and that public governance guidance recognizes disclosure of limitations and ongoing risk management as valid controls. But the controlling policy is specific: current release documentation must reflect current evaluation results, and material segment weaknesses must be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before certification proceeds. The record still shows a material emergency-shelter-placement regression, no approved mitigation or risk acceptance, and no current model card or certification artifact proving the required disclosure is already present. That keeps the certification claim unresolved on a required compliance predicate. This is not noncompliant because the evidence does not prove the disclosure is absent; it proves the certification decision is unsupported on the current record. It is also not compliant_with_caveats, because a caveat can describe a known limitation only when the admissible record shows the caveated certification artifact actually exists. Here, that caveat remains hypothetical rather than evidenced.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and expressly discloses the emergency-shelter-placement regression.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the material subgroup weakness.
The policy predicate for certification remains unresolved on the present record even though aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents.
Prior approval for the model family is contextual only because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and eval batch.
The manual-monitoring note is not reviewed mitigation, approved acceptance, or proof of compliant disclosure.
The actor's narrowed theory depends on a hypothetical or unproven current-release artifact, which cannot support a compliant certification finding on the existing record.
